text: Experiential learning is a learning process in which knowledge is gained through experiences (i.e., hands-on and practical experiences in addition to theory-based components). Experiential learning facilitates learners to create knowledge, skills, and attitudes, and by integrating the experience and perceptions, prompts behaviour change [ 21 ]. The core of experiential learning is David Kolb’s four-stage learning model: (i) concrete experience, in which learners participate in concrete experiences such as hands-on activities, (ii) reflective observation in which learners develop perspectives e.g., reflections of the experiences, (iii) abstract conceptualization whereby learners identify the significance of the learning experience/knowledge and from which new behaviours emerge, and (iv) active experimentation which is the practical application of the new concept [ 22 ]. Reflection is the key component of experiential learning that enables learners to relate knowledge and behaviour in a systematic way [ 23 ]. Experiential learning exposes children to experiences where they can explore, play and become familiar with the materials and concepts that could lead to lifelong learning of the concept [ 24 , 25 ].
